# Disagreement Log — Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 41

**Date:** 2026-03-17
**Agents:** EMET (literal) | LOGOS (formal) | PNEUMA (dynamic)
**Total Disagreements:** 14

---

## Disagreement 1 — 41:1 "remove grief" vs. "put away grief" vs. "get rid of grief"

- **EMET:** "Remove grief from yourself"
- **LOGOS:** "Put away grief from yourself"
- **PNEUMA:** "Get rid of grief"
- **Greek:** *apo sou apobale tēn lypēn* — throw away/cast off grief from yourself
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "Put away grief from yourself" (LOGOS). The compound suggests a decisive casting away; "remove" is less forceful; "get rid of" too colloquial.

---

## Disagreement 2 — 41:1 "most evil" vs. "most pernicious" vs. "most destructive"

- **EMET:** "most evil of all spirits and most ruinous"
- **LOGOS:** "most evil of all spirits, the most pernicious"
- **PNEUMA:** "most destructive of all the spirits"
- **Greek:** *ponērotaton...kai olethriōtaton* — most evil/wicked and most ruinous/destructive
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "most evil...most pernicious" (LOGOS). Preserving both superlatives honors Hermas's rhetorical emphasis. "Pernicious" carries the sense of slow insidious destruction that *olethrios* implies.

---

## Disagreement 3 — 41:1 "wears out the Holy Spirit" — all agree on phrasing

- **EMET:** "wears out the Holy Spirit"
- **LOGOS:** "wearing out the Holy Spirit"
- **PNEUMA:** "wears out the Holy Spirit"
- **Greek:** *ektribei to pneuma to hagion* — rubs out/wears away the Holy Spirit
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA follows EMET/PNEUMA with "wears out." The iterative action of *ektribō* (to rub away) is well captured. LOGOS's participial form is stylistically acceptable but changes the force.

---

## Disagreement 4 — 41:2 "parables" vs. "comparisons"

- **EMET:** "do not comprehend the parables of divinity"
- **LOGOS:** "have no grasp of the comparisons of the divine"
- **PNEUMA:** "can't grasp spiritual teachings"
- **Greek:** *tas parabolas tas theias* — the divine parables/comparisons
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "comparisons of the divine" (LOGOS). *Parabolē* in this context means figurative comparison rather than narrative parable; "comparisons" is more precise. PNEUMA's "spiritual teachings" loses the figurative register.

---

## Disagreement 5 — 41:2 "corrupted and made barren" vs. "corrupted and rendered barren"

- **EMET:** "corrupted and made barren"
- **LOGOS:** "corrupted and rendered barren"
- **PNEUMA:** "warped them and left them spiritually empty"
- **Greek:** *diaphtheirontai kai akarpoi ginomai* — corrupted and becoming fruitless/barren
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "corrupted and rendered barren" (LOGOS). PNEUMA's "spiritually empty" adds a gloss not in the text.

---

## Disagreement 6 — 41:3 "divine" vs. "divinity" — treatment of *theion*

- **EMET:** "inquire concerning divinity and truth"
- **LOGOS:** "inquire concerning the divine and truth"
- **PNEUMA:** "ask real questions about God and truth"
- **Greek:** *peri tou theiou* — concerning the divine/divinity
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "inquire concerning the divine and truth" (LOGOS). The neuter adjective as noun (*to theion*) is a common Greek idiom for the divine realm; "the divine" best represents it.

---

## Disagreement 7 — 41:3 "great understanding" — all agree substantially

- **EMET:** "there also is great understanding"
- **LOGOS:** "there is great understanding"
- **PNEUMA:** "there is deep understanding"
- **Greek:** *synesis megalē* — great understanding/comprehension
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "there is great understanding." *Megalē* means great/large, not "deep." PNEUMA's "deep" is interpretively appropriate but SOPHIA follows the text.

---

## Disagreement 8 — 41:4 "wears out" vs. "exhausts" — treatment in 41:4

- **EMET:** "grief enters into the man and grieves the Holy Spirit and wears it out"
- **LOGOS:** "grief enters the man and grieves the Holy Spirit and wears it out"
- **PNEUMA:** "grief comes into them...distresses the Holy Spirit and exhausts it"
- **Greek:** *lypei to pneuma...ektribei auto* — grieves the Spirit...wears/rubs it out
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "grieves the Holy Spirit and wears it out." EMET and LOGOS agree; "exhausts" (PNEUMA) is acceptable but less precise than "wears out" for *ektribō*.

---

## Disagreement 9 — 41:5 "cleaves to" vs. "settles into"

- **EMET:** "when bitterness cleaves to a man"
- **LOGOS:** "when bitterness cleaves to a man"
- **PNEUMA:** "when bitterness settles into someone"
- **Greek:** *proskollēthē pikria* — sticks/adheres/cleaves to
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "when bitterness cleaves to a man." EMET and LOGOS agree; "cleaves" preserves the adhesive quality of *proskollaō*.

---

## Disagreement 10 — 41:6 "saving grief" treatment

- **EMET:** "grief over sins saves...grief that saves and the grief that destroys"
- **LOGOS:** "this grief over sins is saving...grief that saves and the grief that destroys"
- **PNEUMA:** "grief that saves and the grief that destroys"
- **Greek:** *hē lypē hē sōzōusa* — the saving grief
- **Ruling:** All three agree on the final formula. SOPHIA uses "grief that saves and the grief that destroys" — preserving the antithetical structure.

---

## Disagreement 11 — 41:7 "clothe yourself with cheerfulness" — all agree

- **EMET:** "clothe yourself with cheerfulness"
- **LOGOS:** "clothe yourself with cheerfulness"
- **PNEUMA:** "put on cheerfulness"
- **Greek:** *endysai tēn hilarotēta* — to clothe oneself with cheerfulness
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "clothe yourself with cheerfulness." EMET and LOGOS agree; PNEUMA's "put on" is acceptable but flattens the clothing metaphor.

---

## Disagreement 12 — 41:7 "works lawlessness" vs. "lawless behavior"

- **EMET:** "he works lawlessness"
- **LOGOS:** "he works lawlessness"
- **PNEUMA:** "leads to lawless behavior"
- **Greek:** *anomian ergazetai* — to work/produce lawlessness
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "he works lawlessness." EMET and LOGOS agree; the active construction preserves Hermas's moral agency framing.

---

## Disagreement 13 — 41:8 "mount up to the altar" vs. "ascend to the altar"

- **EMET:** "to ascend to the altar of God"
- **LOGOS:** "to mount up to the altar of God"
- **PNEUMA:** "reaches God's altar"
- **Greek:** *anabēnai pros to thysiasterion tou theou* — to go up to the altar of God
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "mount up to the altar of God" (LOGOS). The spatial ascent imagery is part of Hermas's incense/prayer theology; "mount up" preserves the movement better than "ascend." PNEUMA loses the motion.

---

## Disagreement 14 — 41:8 "pleasant taste" vs. "the same pleasant taste"

- **EMET:** "no longer has the same pleasant taste"
- **LOGOS:** "no longer retains the same pleasant taste"
- **PNEUMA:** "no longer has the same pleasant taste"
- **Greek:** *ouketi echei tēn homoian hēdonēn* — no longer has the same pleasure/pleasantness
- **Ruling:** SOPHIA uses "no longer retains the same pleasant taste" (LOGOS). "Retains" adds the sense of something being held and then lost, which fits the metaphor of wine being adulterated.

---

*End of disagreement log for Shepherd of Hermas Chapter 41.*
